video_title: Warriors can’t overcome another slow start in loss to Pelicans | NBC Sports Bay Area

quotes.speaker: Chris Mullin
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' recurring first-quarter struggles and lack of team discipline
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes you get back in the game, but the Warriors never gained any traction.

text_blocks.speaker: Bonta Hill
text_blocks.text: Mullin, again, first-quarter league, we've seen this in back-to-back nights against San Antonio. They were down 18 nothing before we could blink. Tonight it was 23 to 2 before the Warriors could make a field goal.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mullin
text_blocks.text: Sometimes you get back in the game, but the Warriors never gained any traction. They never led, and the Pelicans from that first quarter on just dictated tempo, pace of play, and their shot-making.

text_blocks.speaker: Festus Ezeli
text_blocks.text: The Warriors, two of 18 from the field and one of 13 from three in the first quarter alone. As you said, Bonta, it is a first-quarter lead, and sometimes you get back in the game, but the Warriors never gained any traction.

quotes.social_post: Chris Mullin notes the Warriors have struggled with recurring first quarter deficits in back to back games. The team never gained any traction against the Pelicans after falling behind early.

structured.context: Chris Mullin analyzes the Warriors' recurring struggles with slow starts in back-to-back losses against San Antonio and New Orleans.

quotes.speaker: Festus Ezeli
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' lack of discipline and poor execution without Steph Curry
quotes.excerpt: These are things that show a lack of discipline right now for the Warriors.
quotes.quote: Having Steph out is a huge detriment to the team because the offense doesn't run the same. But there's a couple of stats that stand out to you. They give up 20 offensive rebounds for 19 points. That's one. They turn the ball over 15 times, give up 27 points. These are things that show a lack of discipline right now for the Warriors. And if you really want to get this ship back on the right track, these are the things that stand out to you. You kind of have to get back into the locker and get back to the drawing board.
quotes.social_post: Festus Ezeli says the Warriors lack discipline without Steph Curry, pointing to 20 offensive rebounds allowed and 15 turnovers as evidence that the team needs to get back to the drawing board.

structured.context: Festus Ezeli discusses the impact of Stephen Curry's absence on the Warriors' discipline and turnover issues.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mullin
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Kerr needs to reconfigure rotation and implement new offensive sets
quotes.excerpt: I think probably now he's going to have to implement a new offense in general.
quotes.quote: With Steph out of the lineup, Steve Kerr has to reconfigure his starting lineup, get the rotations off the bench, and I think probably now he's going to have to implement a new offense in general. Tonight we saw Yaxel at the top of the floor a lot, Draymond was in the corner, and I think it's probably time to go to more set plays to start the possession and then play freelance after that, so everyone has a better feel for where they're supposed to be. You know where the shots come, who you're targeting, who you're going after. That may cut down turnovers because that's a problem. When you have a small margin of error, you have to take care of the basketball, you have to get good shots every time down.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mullin suggests Steve Kerr should implement more set plays to start possessions while Steph Curry is out, arguing it would help the team control the game and cut down on turnovers.

structured.context: Chris Mullin suggests that Steve Kerr should implement more set plays to stabilize the offense while Stephen Curry is sidelined.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mullin
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry's unique gravity and its impact on Warriors' offense
quotes.excerpt: With Steph Curry, when he's on the floor, just by standing out there, he's generating space.
quotes.quote: With Steph Curry, when he's on the floor, just by standing out there, he's generating space and offense for his teammates. So when he's running off screens and they overreact, that's opening up layups, driving lanes. When that's not there, you're looking at a totally different defense. The defense is basically in front of you at all times, and that's why I feel like getting to set plays to start the possession, to control that possession, know where that shot's coming from, understand who you're targeting on the other team's defense, this way you can control the game a little bit, because like you said, it gets out of hand so quickly.
quotes.social_post: Chris Mullin explains that without Steph Curry on the floor, the defense is always in front of the Warriors because they lack the unique gravity that Curry provides.

structured.context: Chris Mullin explains how Stephen Curry's presence on the floor creates space and offensive opportunities for his teammates.

quotes.speaker: Festus Ezeli
quotes.summary_phrase: Yaxel Lendeborg's potential as a focal point for the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: I think the Warriors can still figure it out with Yaxel being the main focal point.
quotes.quote: I think the Warriors can still figure it out with Yaxel being the main focal point. When he became aggressive in the second half, you could just see it. It was like, I'm getting to the rim and you guys can't stop me. Now the Warriors have to figure out a way to use some of that to their advantage where he's driving to the rim, guys are collapsing, and then they're finding open shooters. I thought that's something that's a bright spot for the Warriors, knowing that they have a guy like this they can rely on.
quotes.social_post: Festus Ezeli sees a bright spot in Yaxel Lendeborg, suggesting the Warriors can use his aggression at the rim to collapse defenses and create open shots for teammates.

structured.context: Festus Ezeli highlights Yaxel Lendeborg's potential as an offensive focal point for the Warriors.

quotes.speaker: Brandin Podziemski
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandin Podziemski's need to build chemistry with Yaxel Lendeborg
quotes.excerpt: I'm trying to, as the starting point guard right now, I'm trying to form a great connection.
quotes.quote: If I'm Brandin Podziemski, I'm trying to, as the starting point guard right now, I'm trying to form a great connection with Yaxel. And it's got to be a two-guard, like he and the Yaxel got to have that, you know, the pick and roll like Steph and Draymond have. They have that chemistry. I got to start forming that connection with him because regardless of if Steph is here or not, like you still have to have that. Those guys, they run the bench crew. They're part of the bench mob. They come off a pick and roll, you can create shots that way. I thought Brandin Podziemski in the first half, a lot of what he, the points he brought into the table were points where he was fouled. He was coming off ball screens, they would foul him, and he would get some shots on the board that way. But I think there's a there's another level that he can get to as a point guard right now and running this team.
quotes.social_post: Festus Ezeli says Brandin Podziemski needs to build a pick and roll connection with Yaxel Lendeborg similar to the chemistry between Steph Curry and Draymond Green to help run the offense.

structured.context: Festus Ezeli discusses the need for Brandin Podziemski to develop a pick-and-roll chemistry with Yaxel Lendeborg similar to the duo of Stephen Curry and Draymond Green.
